findings.reason: the consolidation §18 sells does not retire the spelling it thinks it does, and its stated base/head counts are wrong, so the node's own gate cannot pass as written without editing out-of-scope code.
findings.text: §18's done-when claims `grep -rn '== "implementable"' reckon/` reports five sites at the base and exactly one at the head, but `_plan_html.py:353` (`elif status == "implementable":`) also matches, so the tree reports six at the base and two at the head (the `_schema` predicate plus this progress-figure read), and §18 also declines to change that read

findings.reason: the plan should extend or reuse `_plan_html._TAG_RE` (or state why it cannot), rather than add a second raw-text stripper beside it.
findings.text: §16 replaces the prose parser with "a tag-stripper over the slices the reader yields" but names no owner, while `reckon/_plan_html.py` already carries `_TAG_RE = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")` used to strip tags (`_TAG_RE.sub("", ...)` at line 1525), so the plan re-implements tag stripping in the module that owns it

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §17 puts section enumeration, identity and extent behind one public reader `plan_headings` yielding named records over the private `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`, and §16 puts the outstanding-section join behind one module-private predicate over `_section_digests`; the interfaces are small relative to the walk-and-join they hide.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 introduces a raw-text tag-stripper over the reader's slices without citing `reckon/_plan_html.py:1506`'s existing `_TAG_RE`, a tag-stripper in the very module §16 targets.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1477, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds no public definition and says why nothing is retired, §17 adds two and states no public reader can be retired because both keep callers, §18 adds one and states the five readers each keep callers and names; no section adds a CLI option, MCP view or refusal family, and §16 reuses the plan-review-missing family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites the mechanisms it extends (the span parser `reckon/_plan_html.py:44`, `_fingerprint_forms` at `reckon/crew/plan_review.py:598`, the `_schema` declaration enum, and the `interface_counts` module-private rule pattern at `reckon/interface_counts.py:97`), all verified present, but its §18 census of the classification rule is an undercount: it claims five `== "implementable"` sites where the tree has six.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §18's classification predicate is a shared rule its five readers call, not a new layer over live machinery, and it states why the readers cannot merge (each answers a different question); `structured_section_spans` is pre-existing and re-expressed as a projection, not newly wrapped.
